blocks.text: 1. Faithfulness
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863740-601994223.png

Hit Rate closed the retrieval ranking metrics by showing how a floor on retrieval quality caps everything downstream. Faithfulness, whether a generated answer is actually grounded in the retrieved context, shifts this module's focus from measuring retrieval to measuring what generation actually does with it.
It checks each claim in the answer against what the retrieved chunks actually say.
2. Retrieval Metrics Stop At Retrieval
Every metric covered so far in this module stopped at measuring what was retrieved.
None of them check whether the generation model actually used that retrieved context correctly.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric family","What it measures"],"rows":[["Precision, recall, MRR, NDCG, hit rate","What was retrieved"],["Faithfulness","Whether generation actually used the retrieved context"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Breaking The Answer Into Individual Claims

blocks.alt: Breaking The Answer Into Individual Claims
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863740-478296507.png
Similar to how Recursive RAG recursively decomposes a query, a faithfulness check decomposes the generated answer into individual, checkable factual claims.
Each claim then gets verified separately against the retrieved context.
4. Verifying Each Claim Against Context
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863740-297598919.png
Much like Corrective RAG grades retrieved chunks by relevance, each claim here is checked for whether the retrieved context actually supports it.
A claim with no supporting context counts as unfaithful, regardless of whether it happens to be true.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A claim that happens to be factually correct but is not supported by anything in the retrieved context still counts as unfaithful, since faithfulness measures grounding against context, not truth on its own.

blocks.text: 5. Faithfulness Score Is A Fraction
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863741-556094851.png
The faithfulness score is the fraction of claims that are actually supported by the retrieved context.
It is the same fraction based scoring pattern used by precision, applied here to generation instead of retrieval.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Claims in answer","Faithfulness score"],"rows":[["4 out of 5 claims supported","0.8"],["5 out of 5 claims supported","1.0"]]}

blocks.text: 6. Faithfulness Is Independent Of Retrieval Quality

blocks.alt: Faithfulness Is Independent Of Retrieval Quality
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863741-3204079.png
Just as high precision in Precision At K can still mean a missed answer, a retrieval system with perfect precision can still feed a generation model that ignores the retrieved context anyway.
Faithfulness measures a completely separate failure mode from retrieval quality.
7. Faithfulness Does Not Check Factual Accuracy
A claim can be perfectly grounded in the retrieved context and still be factually wrong, if the source itself was wrong.
Faithfulness measures grounding, not truth.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: An answer that faithfully repeats an error already present in the retrieved source document still scores perfectly on faithfulness, since faithfulness only checks whether the claim matches the context, not whether the context itself was correct.

blocks.text: 8. Measuring Faithfulness Requires A Judge Model

blocks.alt: Measuring Faithfulness Requires A Judge Model
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863939-625541113.png
As with the grader model in Corrective RAG, checking whether a claim is supported usually requires another model to make that judgment.
Automated faithfulness scoring adds its own evaluation cost and its own possible errors.
9. Recognizing When Faithfulness Is Worth Measuring Directly

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Faithfulness Is Worth Measuring Directly
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863940-510832802.png
A system where ungrounded claims are unacceptable needs faithfulness scoring.
A system where retrieval quality alone already predicts good answers, by contrast, may not need the added faithfulness check.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates decomposing an answer into claims and scoring faithfulness against the retrieved context.

code.content:
context = "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month and includes ten projects."

answer_claims = [
    "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month.",
    "The Falcon plan includes ten projects.",
    "The Falcon plan offers a free trial.",
]

def is_supported(claim, context):
    # checks whether a claim's key terms appear in the context
    key_terms = [term for term in claim.lower().split() if len(term) > 4]
    matches = sum(1 for term in key_terms if term in context.lower())
    return matches >= 2

def faithfulness_score(claims, context):
    # the fraction of claims that are supported
    supported = [claim for claim in claims if is_supported(claim, context)]
    return len(supported) / len(claims), supported

score, supported_claims = faithfulness_score(answer_claims, context)

print("Faithfulness check:")
for claim in answer_claims:
    status = "supported" if claim in supported_claims else "unsupported"
    print(f"  [{status}] {claim}")

print(f"\nFaithfulness score: {score:.2f}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the free trial claim scoring unsupported since nothing in the context mentions it, regardless of whether a free trial actually exists.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Assuming a high faithfulness score also guarantees the answer is factually correct.
Skipping faithfulness measurement because retrieval precision and recall already look good.
Treating a claim as supported just because it is topically related to the context.
Forgetting that automated faithfulness scoring itself needs a judge model with its own error rate.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Faithfulness measures whether a generated answer is actually grounded in the retrieved context.
Retrieval metrics stop at what was retrieved; faithfulness checks what generation did with it.
A faithfulness check decomposes the answer into individual, checkable factual claims.
Each claim is verified against the retrieved context; unsupported claims count as unfaithful.
The faithfulness score is the fraction of claims actually supported by the retrieved context.
Faithfulness is independent of retrieval quality; perfect retrieval can still feed an unfaithful answer.
Faithfulness measures grounding, not truth; a faithfully repeated source error still scores well.
Measuring faithfulness usually requires a separate judge model, adding its own cost and error rate.
